atoms.text: This guide configures the MirrorLane replication service to copy new objects from the bucket app-data-primary to the bucket app-data-dr for disaster recovery. Both buckets and the replication role belong to account 111122223333. Create an IAM role named mirrorlane-replicator and set its trust policy to allow the MirrorLane service principal to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetReplicationConfiguration and s3:ListBucket on app-data-primary, s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication on app-data-primary/*, and s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateDelete on app-data-dr/*. Because the role and both buckets are in the same account, this identity-based policy alone grants the required access, and the bucket policy on app-data-dr is left unchanged. Enable versioning on both buckets, since replication requires it. Create a replication rule on app-data-primary that covers the whole bucket, sets app-data-dr as the destination, and specifies the role ARN. Upload a test object and confirm that its replication status changes from PENDING to COMPLETED and that the replica appears in app-data-dr with the same key and version metadata.

This guide configures the MirrorLane replication service to copy new objects from the bucket app-data-primary to the bucket app-data-dr for disaster recovery. The source bucket and the replication role belong to account 111122223333, while app-data-dr is owned by account 444455556666. In account 111122223333, create an IAM role named mirrorlane-replicator and set its trust policy to allow the MirrorLane service principal to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetReplicationConfiguration and s3:ListBucket on app-data-primary and s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication on app-data-primary/*. Because the destination bucket is in a different account, the owner of account 444455556666 must add a statement to the bucket policy of app-data-dr that names the role arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/mirrorlane-replicator as the principal and allows s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateDelete on app-data-dr/*. Enable versioning on both buckets, since replication requires it. Create a replication rule on app-data-primary that covers the whole bucket, sets app-data-dr as the destination, and specifies the role ARN. Upload a test object and confirm that its replication status changes from PENDING to COMPLETED and that the replica appears in app-data-dr with the same key and version metadata.

This guide grants the SnapVault backup agent write access to the bucket db-backups, where it stores nightly database snapshot archives under the prefix nightly/. The agent runs on hosts in account 111122223333, and the bucket is owned by the same account. Create an IAM role named snapvault-writer and attach it to the instance profile used by the backup hosts. Add an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload, and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on db-backups/nightly/*, and s3:ListBucket on db-backups restricted to the nightly/ prefix. Since the role and the bucket share an account, this identity-based policy is the only grant needed, and the bucket policy of db-backups is not modified. Configure the agent with the bucket name, the prefix, and a multipart part size of 64 MiB. Run a manual backup and check that a single archive named with the snapshot timestamp appears under nightly/. Verify that the agent can list but not overwrite or delete earlier archives, which confirms that the policy is scoped as intended.

This guide grants the SnapVault backup agent write access to the bucket db-backups, where it stores nightly database snapshot archives under the prefix nightly/. The agent runs on hosts in account 111122223333, and the bucket is owned by account 444455556666. Create an IAM role named snapvault-writer in account 111122223333 and attach it to the instance profile used by the backup hosts. Add an identity-based policy to the role that allows the same write actions on db-backups/nightly/*. The owner of account 444455556666 then adds a bucket policy statement that names arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/snapvault-writer as the principal and allows s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload, and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on db-backups/nightly/*, and s3:ListBucket restricted to the nightly/ prefix. Configure the agent with the bucket name, the prefix, and a multipart part size of 64 MiB. Run a manual backup and check that a single archive named with the snapshot timestamp appears under nightly/. Verify that the agent can list but not overwrite or delete earlier archives, which confirms that the policy is scoped as intended.

This guide gives the RestoreRunner job read access to the bucket vm-image-backups so it can retrieve virtual machine image backups during recovery. The job runs in account 111122223333, and the bucket is in the same account. Create an IAM role named restorerunner-reader and set its trust policy to allow the RestoreRunner service to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on vm-image-backups/images/*, and s3:ListBucket and s3:GetBucketLocation on vm-image-backups. Because the role and the bucket are owned by one account, no bucket policy statement is added, and the existing bucket policy stays as it is. In the RestoreRunner console, select the role and specify the images/ prefix as the restore source. Start a test restore of one image and monitor the transfer until the job reports a matching checksum. Confirm that the image is written to the local staging volume and that the bucket contents are unchanged afterward.

This guide gives the RestoreRunner job read access to the bucket vm-image-backups so it can retrieve virtual machine image backups during recovery. The job runs in account 111122223333, and the bucket is owned by account 444455556666. Create an IAM role named restorerunner-reader in account 111122223333 and set its trust policy to allow the RestoreRunner service to assume it. The owner of account 444455556666 adds a bucket policy statement that names the account ID 111122223333 as the principal and allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on vm-image-backups/images/*, and s3:ListBucket and s3:GetBucketLocation on vm-image-backups. The role's own identity-based policy must also allow these same read actions on that bucket. In the RestoreRunner console, select the role and specify the images/ prefix as the restore source. Start a test restore of one image and monitor the transfer until the job reports a matching checksum. Confirm that the image is written to the local staging volume and that the bucket contents are unchanged afterward.

This guide gives a backup administrator, the IAM user backup-admin-ops, access to download and inspect recovery points stored in the bucket dr-recovery-points. The user and the bucket are both in account 111122223333. Recovery points are stored under the prefix points/ and are read through the command-line client when an integrity review is required. Attach an identity-based policy to the user that allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on dr-recovery-points/points/*, and s3:ListBucket and s3:ListBucketVersions on dr-recovery-points. Because the user and the bucket belong to the same account, the identity-based policy carries the whole grant, and the bucket policy is not changed. Configure the client with the user's access key and set the default region to the bucket's region. List the points/ prefix and download one recovery point to a local directory. Compare the downloaded object's checksum with the value recorded in its metadata and confirm that no write or delete request is allowed for this user.

This guide gives a backup administrator, the IAM user backup-admin-ops, access to download and inspect recovery points stored in the bucket dr-recovery-points. The user belongs to account 111122223333, and the bucket is owned by account 444455556666. Recovery points are stored under the prefix points/ and are read through the command-line client when an integrity review is required. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement that names arn:aws:iam::111122223333:user/backup-admin-ops as the principal and allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on dr-recovery-points/points/*, and s3:ListBucket and s3:ListBucketVersions on dr-recovery-points. The user's identity-based policy in account 111122223333 must also allow these read actions on the same resources. Configure the client with the user's access key and set the default region to the bucket's region. List the points/ prefix and download one recovery point to a local directory. Compare the downloaded object's checksum with the value recorded in its metadata and confirm that no write or delete request is allowed for this user.

This guide sets up the TrailKeeper service to copy audit log files from the bucket log-staging to the bucket audit-archive, where they are kept for long-term retention. TrailKeeper reads objects under the prefix audit/ and writes them to the same prefix in the archive bucket using the STANDARD_INFREQUENT storage class. The role, both buckets, and the audit pipeline are in account 111122223333. Create an IAM role named trailkeeper-copier and attach an identity-based policy that allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on log-staging, and s3:PutObject on audit-archive/audit/*. As everything is in one account, this identity-based policy provides all required access, and neither bucket policy is edited. Set the TrailKeeper copy schedule to run every 15 minutes and mark copied objects with the tag copied=true. Trigger a manual run after placing a sample log file in log-staging/audit/. Verify that the file appears in audit-archive/audit/ with the expected storage class and an identical size.

This guide sets up the TrailKeeper service to copy audit log files from the bucket log-staging to the bucket audit-archive, where they are kept for long-term retention. TrailKeeper reads objects under the prefix audit/ and writes them to the same prefix in the archive bucket using the STANDARD_INFREQUENT storage class. The role and log-staging belong to account 111122223333, while audit-archive is owned by account 444455556666. Create an IAM role named trailkeeper-copier in account 111122223333 and attach an identity-based policy that allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on log-staging. The owner of account 444455556666 adds a bucket policy statement to audit-archive that names arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/trailkeeper-copier as the principal and allows s3:PutObject on audit-archive/audit/*. Set the TrailKeeper copy schedule to run every 15 minutes and mark copied objects with the tag copied=true. Trigger a manual run after placing a sample log file in log-staging/audit/. Verify that the file appears in audit-archive/audit/ with the expected storage class and an identical size.

This guide grants the IntegrityCheck service access to the bucket backup-vault so it can verify stored backups and publish its findings. IntegrityCheck reads each backup object and its checksum manifest under the prefix sets/, then writes a verification report under the prefix verify-reports/ in the same bucket. The service role and the bucket are in account 111122223333. Create an IAM role named integritycheck-runner and attach an identity-based policy that allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectAttributes on backup-vault/sets/*, s3:PutObject on backup-vault/verify-reports/*, and s3:ListBucket on backup-vault. Because the role and the bucket share an account, the bucket policy is not modified, and the identity-based policy is the only source ofthe grant. Define a verification schedule of once per week and set the sample rate to 10 percent of objects. Run a verification job against one backup set. Open the generated report in verify-reports/ and confirm that it lists each checked object with a pass or fail result.

This guide grants the IntegrityCheck service access to the bucket backup-vault so it can verify stored backups and publish its findings. IntegrityCheck reads each backup object and its checksum manifest under the prefix sets/, then writes a verification report under the prefix verify-reports/ in the same bucket. The service role is in account 111122223333, and the bucket is owned by account 444455556666. Create an IAM role named integritycheck-runner in account 111122223333 and attach an identity-based policy that allows the same read, write, and list actions on backup-vault. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement that names arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/integritycheck-runner as the principal and allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectAttributes on backup-vault/sets/*, s3:PutObject on backup-vault/verify-reports/*, and s3:ListBucket on backup-vault. Define a verification schedule of once per week and set the sample rate to 10 percent of objects. Run a verification job against one backup set. Open the generated report in verify-reports/ and confirm that it lists each checked object with a pass or fail result.

This guide configures the PruneWorker service to remove expired backup versions from the bucket archive-retention according to a 90-day retention rule. PruneWorker lists object versions under the prefix expired-candidates/ and deletes any version older than the retention limit. The worker's role and the bucket are both in account 111122223333. Create an IAM role named pruneworker-deleter and attach an identity-based policy that allows s3:ListBucketVersions on archive-retention, and s3:DeleteObject and s3:DeleteObjectVersion on archive-retention/expired-candidates/*. Since the role and the bucket are in the same account, this policy is the complete grant and the bucket policy is left untouched. Set the PruneWorker retention value to 90 days and enable dry-run mode for the first execution. Review the dry-run output to confirm that only versions older than 90 days are listed. Disable dry-run mode and confirm that the deleted versions no longer appear in a version listing of the prefix.

This guide configures the PruneWorker service to remove expired backup versions from the bucket archive-retention according to a 90-day retention rule. PruneWorker lists object versions under the prefix expired-candidates/ and deletes any version older than the retention limit. The worker's role is in account 111122223333, and the bucket is owned by account 444455556666. Create an IAM role named pruneworker-deleter in account 111122223333 with an identity-based policy that permits the same list and delete actions on archive-retention. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement that names arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/pruneworker-deleter as the principal and allows s3:ListBucketVersions on archive-retention, and s3:DeleteObject and s3:DeleteObjectVersion on archive-retention/expired-candidates/*. Set the PruneWorker retention value to 90 days and enable dry-run mode for the first execution. Review the dry-run output to confirm that only versions older than 90 days are listed. Disable dry-run mode and confirm that the deleted versions no longer appear in a version listing of the prefix.

This guide sets up the BulkResync batch job to copy objects that existed in the bucket orders-primary before replication was enabled into the bucket orders-secondary. BulkResync reads a manifest file listing the keys to copy, reads each source object, and writes a copy with the same key to the secondary bucket. The batch role and both buckets belong to account 111122223333. Create an IAM role named bulkresync-copier and attach an identity-based policy that allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on orders-primary/*, s3:GetObject on the manifest location orders-primary/manifests/*, and s3:PutObject on orders-secondary/*. Because all resources are in one account, the identity-based policy provides all access, and neither bucket policy is changed. Submit a job that references the manifest, the role ARN, and a completion report location. Wait for the job status to reach Complete and review the report for failed keys. Spot-check several keys in orders-secondary to confirm that sizes and ETags match the source objects.

BulkResync reads a manifest file listing the keys to copy, reads each source object, and writes a copy with the same key to the secondary bucket. The batch role and orders-primary belong to account 111122223333, while orders-secondary is owned by account 444455556666. Create an IAM role named bulkresync-copier in account 111122223333 and attach an identity-based policy that allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on orders-primary/*, and s3:GetObject on orders-primary/manifests/*. The owner of account 444455556666 adds a bucket policy statement to orders-secondary that names arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/bulkresync-copier as the principal and allows s3:PutObject on orders-secondary/*. Submit a job that references the manifest, the role ARN, and a completion report location. Wait for the job status to reach Complete and review the report for failed keys. Spot-check several keys in orders-secondary to confirm that sizes and ETags match the source objects.
